mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE increases > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS declines for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to increased corporate profits and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which typically leads to lower borrowing costs and increased investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS decreases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS increases > 200,000 jobs.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real final sales (RSAFS) signals a strengthening demand side of the economy, which typically leads to increased corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS increase.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to reduced investment and consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS increases > 0.25% during a tightening cycle.
